Based on the retrieved healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that both hepatitis G virus (HGV) and TT virus (HTT) have been investigated for their potential involvement in cryptogenic chronic liver disease. However, the available data suggest that HGV is more likely to be involved.

In Southern Italy, where one of the matched questions was retrieved, HGV infection has been found to be widespread among patients with chronic hepatitis, independently of parenteral risk factors. This indicates a strong association between HGV and chronic liver disease. Furthermore, in the context of cryptogenic liver disease, HGV's frequency is comparable to that observed in chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) chronic liver disease.

In contrast, HTT infection is relatively uncommon among patients with cryptogenic or HCV-related liver disease who do not have a history of parenteral exposure. This suggests that while HTT may be involved in some cases of liver disease, it appears to play a lesser role compared to HGV in the context of cryptogenic chronic liver disease.

Therefore, based on the available data and findings from the matched questions, hepatitis G virus (HGV) is likely to be more closely associated with cryptogenic chronic liver disease than TT virus infection.
